args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service started failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. I rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Checked after the rollback: all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression, and look at why a release that was unhealthy in staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
checkout-api is rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions and is healthy again. I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Cause:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with about 18% of requests erroring.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to that. I checked afterwards: all three regions are running v2.3.0, the service reports healthy and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the post-rollback check. It suggests finding the root cause of the v2.3.1 problem. It also points out that the test version of this release (v2.3.1-rc) was already unhealthy in staging but still went to production, which is worth looking into.

content.text: The most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
